components.name: dti
components.method: 0.333·placement + 0.667·anchor (λ at n=3): placement of DeckCheck's score (of 96) within bracket 4; anchor = the mean of its twelve rubric grades (S 100, A 75, B 50, C 25, F 0); draw Normal(anchor, DTI_PRIOR_READ_SD = 4.0, a declared prior (one reading on this list)); an LLM's dated read of card quality, never ours

limits: A rating is ★ coaching over ◆ inputs; the score never gates. The floor (bracket_report.json) is the only bracket gate.
calibrate.py refuses a verdict below 10 decks with 20 games each; no figure here is checked against outcomes yet (`rating --calibrate` reports the refusal with today's n).

Goldfish kill is one column, never the rule: the benchmark is an unopposed ceiling with no blockers and no removal, and a combo or control deck reads slow for not attacking; a win the goldfish cannot see (`alt_win_cards`) multiplies speed's weight by 0.5.
Forge is not a power read until the harness work is done (the pilot's rule, 2026-10-18): its component ships at weight 0.00 and is shown only for a run on the current list.

DeckCheck's Threat Index is a component at prior weight 0.15 (2026-10-19): one LLM's dated read of card quality, withheld when it describes another list; its interval is a declared prior sd of 4.0 on the anchor until three decks carry two readings on one list; its score places within the bracket, its twelve rubric grades anchor.
Diagnostic engine figures are read against each deck's own declaration and are never ranked across decks; they are evidence for the argument, not a component.

The weights are a Dirichlet prior (κ = 20.0) and the inputs are drawn from their posteriors: `score` is the median of 2000 seeded draws, `score_ci` its 90% interval, and every sd in `uncertainty` is declared, not estimated.
A placement within a group of n is a (n−1)-point scale and earns the share λ = (n−1)/(n−1+4) of its component, the rest going to the cited anchor; at n=3 that is one third.
A divergent `concordance` — the deck's instruments rank it far apart — prints the grade as a range, never a letter, and the judgment must address every outlier instrument.
rank over n=3 decks; no significance claim

findings.note: 65 equals code_score 65.1 (rounded); claims no gap. Scorecard re-run is identical on components, withheld, code_score, score_point, bracket, limits, uncertainty, sensitivity. Nothing below is claimed, and resilience (40, placement 0, 14 answer cards, 2 classes) is scored once.

judgment.argument: What the measured components cannot see here is play. No game is logged on this list, no survey, no Forge run on it, and the only game on record was played before the changes that gave the deck its answers, so it speaks to none of them. The goldfish has no blockers or removal, so its speed reading (kill_by_turn_8 0.898) is a ceiling, not a table result. The branch toward Torbran and wheels that also remove met its stated objective and the pilot's notes list what is still to test: whether the new answers get cast, whether the commanders arrive on time without added ramp, and whether Torbran's bonus turns wheels into kills against real removal. Those are open questions, not facts I can score either way. The two outliers are DeckCheck's Threat Index and resilience, both on the worse side. I cannot say which to believe. Resilience is already carried in full by the components (14 answer cards, two classes answered), and the record has no game showing whether the new answers work, so nothing unmeasured justifies moving it. The record also does not explain DeckCheck's reading. For both, my number sits at code_score. It is no higher because nothing has been played on this list, and no lower because every weakness I could name is already a component.
